name: Mean sentence-length variance
instruction: Measure how much sentence length varies across the story: compute roughly how far sentence lengths spread around their average. Score 1.0 when lengths vary a great deal (very short sentences mixed with very long ones), 0.5 for moderate variation, 0.0 when nearly all sentences are of similar length. Measure the variation only; pay no attention to whether any variation is purposeful or achieves an effect.
rationale: PLANTED PROBE (coordinator-authored). Shallow statistical counterpart of R6A07 'Deliberate sentence rhythm': length variance is the measurable residue of rhythm while measuring nothing about deliberateness or effect. Note this probe is deliberately adjacent to the lineation family the reviewer challenged, so it also tests whether the auditor keeps counting the surface trace on the nuisance side when its craft twin is in the same pool.

name: Distinct-adjective type count
instruction: Count how many DIFFERENT adjectives the story uses (count each distinct adjective once, however often it recurs). Score 1.0 for a very large vocabulary of distinct adjectives, 0.5 for a moderate one, 0.0 for very few. Count the vocabulary only; pay no attention to whether any description is precise, apt, or earns its place.
rationale: PLANTED PROBE (coordinator-authored). Shallow lexical counterpart of R6A04 'Embodied sensory and physical grounding': adjective-type richness is the vocabulary residue of descriptive writing while measuring nothing about whether the body and senses are actually present on the page.
